en: *Catalogue of the Scriptures*, Fascicle One, compiled by Shi Jingtai.
Single-text and single-source works: originally one version, with no further separate translations; totaling four hundred and forty-one works in two thousand seven hundred and eight fascicles.
Mahāyāna sūtras in thirteen fascicles; single-fascicle Mahāyāna sūtras, one hundred and ninety-one works totaling one thousand two hundred and sixty-two fascicles;

the *Buddhāvataṃsaka-mahāvaipulya-sūtra*, sixty fascicles totaling one thousand eighty-seven sheets, translated in the Yixi era of the Jin dynasty by Buddhabhadra together with Faye and others at Yangzhou in fifty fascicles;
and the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, forty fascicles totaling seven hundred and twenty sheets.
During the Northern Liang dynasty, Dharmakṣema, together with Huìsōng and others, translated the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* in six hundred fascicles and twelve thousand sheets at Guzang.
During the Tang dynasty, Xuánzàng translated the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* in forty fascicles (or thirty fascicles) and six hundred nineteen sheets at Yuhua Palace.

During the Later Qin dynasty, Kumārajīva, together with Sēngruì and others, translated [the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*]—also known as the *Mahāvaipulya-mahāsannipāta-sūtra*—in thirty fascicles and six hundred four sheets at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng’ān.
In Guzang, during the Northern Liang dynasty, Dharmakṣema translated the *Mahāvaipulya-sūryagarbha-sūtra* in ten fascicles (or fifteen fascicles), totaling two hundred and four sheets.
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, Ratnayaśas translated the *Mahāvaipulya-candragarbha-sūtra* at Daxingshan Temple in ten fascicles, totaling two hundred and fourteen sheets.
During the Qi dynasty, Ratnayaśas, together with Fazhi, translated the *Ratnajvalā-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in ten fascicles, totaling one hundred and thirty sheets.
The *Mahātejas-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in twenty fascicles and two hundred sixty-five sheets was translated by Prajñāmitra and others at the Jetavana Monastery during the Zhenguan era of the Tang dynasty.

The *Dharmolkā-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in twenty fascicles and three hundred sheets was submitted for imperial circulation during the reign of the present dynasty; it was translated by Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta at the Xingshan Monastery during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.

The *Mahābodhisattvapiṭaka-sūtra* in twenty fascicles and four hundred ten sheets was submitted for imperial circulation during the reign of the present dynasty; it was translated by Dharmagupta at the Shanglin Garden in the Eastern Capital during the Daye era of the Sui dynasty.
During the Zhenguan era, Xuanzang translated the *Bodhisattvamaṇikūṭarāja-sūtra* in twelve fascicles (330 sheets) at Hongfu Monastery;
alternatively, it exists in fourteen fascicles.
During the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin dynasty, Zhu Fonian translated the *Bodhisattvadṛṣṭatattvasamādhi-sūtra* in fourteen fascicles (238 sheets) in Chang’an.
The *Buddhanāmasūtra* in twelve fascicles and two hundred forty-seven sheets was translated by Jñānayaśas during the Qi dynasty.
The *Candrapradīpasamādhisūtra* in ten (or eleven) fascicles and two hundred three sheets was translated by Bodhiruci at Xiangzhou during the Northern Wei dynasty.
The *Bhadrakalpikasūtra* in thirteen fascicles and one hundred ninety-five sheets was translated by Jñānayaśas together with Fazhi during the Tiāntǒng era of the Qi dynasty.
The *Huashou jing* (Flower-Hand Sūtra) in ten fascicles and two hundred fifteen sheets, translated by Zhu Fahu during the Yuankang era of the Jin dynasty;

the *Shizhu duanjie jing* (Sūtra on the Ten Stages and Severing Bonds) in ten fascicles and two hundred fifty-four sheets, translated by Kumārajīva at the Great Monastery in Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty;

and the *Daguanding jing* (Great Consecration Sūtra) in twelve fascicles and one hundred thirteen sheets, translated by Zhu Fonian together with Dao’an during the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin dynasty.
The *Buddhanusmṛtisamādhisūtra* in ten fascicles (or eight fascicles), totaling one hundred fifty-nine sheets, was translated during the Jin dynasty by Śrīmitra.
The *Pañcasahasrapañcaśatabuddhanāmasūtra* in eight fascicles, totaling one hundred twenty-six sheets, was translated at Yangzhou during the Yongchu era of the Song dynasty by Buddhabhadra.
The [text] in question was translated at Xingshan Monastery during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty by Jñānagupta, Dharmagupta, and others.

The *Dafangbian bao'en jing* (Sūtra on the Great Expedient Means for Repaying Kindness) in seven fascicles and one hundred twenty-four sheets; the *Dafangdeng daji jing* (Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra) in eight fascicles and one hundred twenty-eight sheets;

the *Shengtianwang bore boluomi jing* (Śrīmaladevī-siṃhanāda-prajñāpāramitā Sūtra) in seven fascicles and one hundred twenty-one sheets—these were translated by the prince of the Yuezhi kingdom, Puṣya, during the Chen dynasty at Yangzhou. The *Baoyun jing* (Ratnamegha Sūtra) in seven fascicles and one hundred sheets—or in seven or eight fascicles—was translated by Mandra of Liang at Yangzhou.
The *Jinguangming jing* (Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra) in six fascicles—or in seven or eight fascicles—and one hundred twenty-two sheets.

The *Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra* in eight fascicles (or seven or six fascicles), totaling one hundred twenty-one sheets, was translated during the Northern Liang dynasty by Dharmakṣema and later during the Chen dynasty by Paramārtha.
The *Bodhisattvagarbha-sūtra* in five fascicles, totaling one hundred thirteen sheets, was translated at Luoyang during the Later Wei dynasty by Bodhiruci.
The *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra* in five fascicles, totaling eighty-eight sheets, was translated at Chang’an during the Former Qin dynasty by Zhu Fonian.
During the Tiāntóng era of the Qi dynasty, Dharmayaśas and Fazhi translated the *Mahāsannipāta-Bhadrapāla-bodhisattva-sūtra* in five (or six) fascicles, comprising ninety-three pages.

During the Kaihuáng era of the Sui dynasty, Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta translated it at Dàxīngshàn Temple; this imperial edition was circulated as the *Mahāvaipulya-nirnimitta-sūtra* in six fascicles, also known as the *Mahāmegha-sūtra*, comprising ninety-two pages.
During the Former Qin, Zhu Fonian translated the *Guhyapada-vajrapāṇi-sūtra* in five (or four) fascicles, comprising one hundred twelve pages.
The *Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra* in four (or five) fascicles and sixty-two pages, translated by Zhu Fahu during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty;
the *Sāgaranāgarāja-paripṛcchā Sūtra* in four fascicles and seventy-two pages, translated by Facong in the Gaochang commandery during the Northern Liang period;
and the *Aṅgulimālīya Sūtra* in four fascicles and seventy-eight pages, translated by Dharmakṣema during the Northern Liang period.
During the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty, Guṇabhadra translated the *Asarvabhāva-bodhisattva-sūtra* in four fascicles (sixty sheets) at Yangzhou.
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, Jñānagupta, Dharmagupta, and others translated the *Saṃghāṭa-sūtra* in four fascicles (fifty-one sheets) at Daxingshan Temple;
it was subsequently submitted for circulation by the Imperial Court.
*The Scripture on the Contemplation of All Dharmas*, four fascicles, sixty sheets; translated during the Northern Wei dynasty by the Yuezhi monk Baoshouna.
Translated at Daxingshan Temple during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty by Jñānagupta, Dharmagupta, and others;

submitted for circulation by the Imperial Court. *The Scripture on the Divine Mantras of the Seven Buddhas*, four fascicles, seventy sheets. *The Scripture on the Original Deeds of the Bodhisattva*, three fascicles, fifty-two sheets. *The Scripture on the Praise of the Merits of All Buddhas*, three fascicles, fifty-five sheets.
The *Bodhisattvapitaka-sūtra* in three fascicles and sixty-one sheets, translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin;
the *Baladharāṇasamādhi-sūtra* in three fascicles and thirty-six sheets, translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin;
and the *Sujātadevaputra-sūtra* in three or four fascicles and forty-six sheets, translated by Dharmayaśas during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
The *Śūraṅgama-samādhi Sūtra*, three fascicles (or two fascicles), fifty-two sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taishi era of the Jin dynasty.
The *Pratyutpanna-samādhi Sūtra*, three fascicles (or two fascicles), forty-seven sheets; translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
The *Samādhirāja-sūtra* (or *Bodhisattvapṛcchā-samādhi Sūtra*), two fascicles (or three fascicles), fifty sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Fifty Comparisons of the Perfection of Wisdom*, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty: two fascicles, forty sheets.
*The Scripture on the Original Acts of the Bodhisattva’s Diadem*, translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty: two fascicles, forty-eight sheets.
*The Scripture of the Bodhisattva Protector of the Nation*, translated by Zhu Fonian during the Former Qin dynasty: two fascicles, forty-three sheets.
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, Jñānagupta, Guptaka, and others translated the *Sūryavairocanasamādhi-sūtra* in two fascicles (forty-six sheets) at Daxingshan Temple;
this was submitted for circulation by the imperial court.
During the Taishi era of the Jin dynasty, Dharmarakṣa translated the *Candrottarādārikā-sūtra* in two fascicles (twenty-seven sheets).
*The Sūtra on the Intermediate State* (Antarābhava-sūtra), two fascicles, twenty-seven sheets; translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Storehouse of Mount Sumeru* (Sumerugarbha-sūtra), two fascicles, thirty-eight sheets; translated by Zhu Fonian in Chang’an during the reign of Former Qin.

*The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Entry into the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata within the Flower Ornament* (Buddhāvataṃsaka-tathāgataguṇajñānācintyaviṣayāvatāra-nirdeśa-sūtra), one fascicle, twenty-eight sheets; translated by Dharmayaśas together with Fazhi during the Qi dynasty.

During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, Jñānagupta, Guptadatta, and others translated the *Mahābherīhāraka-sūtra* (The Great Dharma Drum Sutra) in two fascicles and forty sheets at Daxingshan Temple; this was submitted for imperial circulation.
During the Song dynasty, Guṇavarman translated the *Sarvabuddhaparigraha-sūtra* (The Essential Collection of All Buddhas) in two fascicles and forty-two sheets at Yangzhou.
*Mañjuśrī-buddhakṣetra-vyūha-sūtra*, two fascicles, thirty-four sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty in Luoyang in the Yongxi era.
*Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra* (also titled *Sarvadharmā-māyopama-samādhi-nirṇaya-sūtra*), two fascicles; translated by Dharmarakṣa in Luoyang during the Yongxi era of the Jin dynasty.
*Mahāyāna-samatā-nirdeśa-sūtra*, two fascicles, thirty-nine sheets; translated by Master Xiang in Nanhai Commandery during the Song dynasty.
During the Tiānhé era of the Later Zhou dynasty, Jñānagupta, together with Seng’an, translated the *Mahāsannipāta-dṛṣṭāntarāja-sūtra* in two fascicles, comprising thirty-two sheets.
During the Kāihuáng era of the Sui dynasty, Jñānagupta, together with Seng’an and Guptadatta and others, translated it at Dàxīngshàn Monastery;

this was subsequently submitted for imperial circulation as the *Akṣobhyatathāgatasyavyūha-sūtra* in two fascicles, also titled the *Buddhakṣetraprasiddhabodhisattvaśikṣā-sūtra*, comprising thirty-eight sheets.
During the Jianhe era of the Later Han, Zhi Chen translated the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīkamukha-sūtra* in two fascicles and twenty-two sheets.
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, Jñānayaśas translated the *Kāśyapa-sūtra* in two fascicles and thirty-nine sheets.
During the Northern Wei period, Upaśūna translated the *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in two fascicles and forty-two sheets.
The *Pratibhāsa-viśuddha-citta-sūtra* in two fascicles and twenty-seven sheets was translated by Saṃghabara during the Liang dynasty.
The *Anuttarāśraya-sūtra* in two fascicles and thirty-one sheets was translated by Jñānagupta, Guptadatta, and others at Daxingshan Monastery during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty;
it was subsequently submitted for imperial circulation by the present dynasty.
The Śramaṇa Paramārtha translated the *Vijñānasaṃkrānti-sūtra* in two fascicles (thirty-three pages) at Guangzhou during the Chen dynasty.
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, Jñānagupta, Dharmagupta, and others translated the *Adbhutadharmaparyāya-sūtra* in two fascicles (forty pages) at Daxingshan Temple;
it was subsequently submitted for imperial circulation by the Royal Court.

During the Southern Qi dynasty, Tanjing translated: *The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra*, two fascicles (or three), fifty-one pages; *The Sūtra of Inconceivable Merit*, two fascicles, also known as the *Sūtra of Merit*, thirty-eight pages; *The Sūtra of Great Auspicious Meaning and Dhāraṇī*, two fascicles (or four), thirty-eight pages; *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva’s Dream*, two fascicles, also known as the *Sūtra of Auspicious Responses*, thirty-four pages; *The Sūtra of the Samādhi of Tranquil Illumination*, one fascicle, thirteen pages.

During the Tang Dynasty, Xuanzang translated the *Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-sūtra* in two fascicles (49 sheets), the *Ratnarāśi-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* in two fascicles (28 sheets), the *Dharmadhātusvabhāva-avikalpa-sūtra* in two fascicles (24 sheets), the *Guhyakapada-vajrapāṇi-sūtra* in two fascicles (36 sheets), the *Mahāvaipulya-tathāgataguhyagarbha-sūtra* in two fascicles (24 sheets), and the *Subāhu-bodhisattvaparikṣā-sūtra* in two fascicles (26 sheets). During the Kaihuang era of the Sui Dynasty, Śīlādharagupta and others translated the *Sarvadharma-agrarāja-sūtra* in one fascicle (12 sheets) at Daxingshan Monastery;
during the same Kaihuang era, Śīlādharagupta and Dharmagupta and others translated [the same] at Daxingshan Monastery. The *Sarvadharma-agrarāja-sūtra* consists of one fascicle (22 sheets).
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui Dynasty, Śīlādharagupta and Dharmagupta and others translated it at Daxingshan Monastery.
*Chengju guangming dingyi jing* (Sūtra on the Attainment of the Radiant Concentrated Intention), one fascicle, twenty-two sheets;
translated by Zhi Yao during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty. *Taizi xuda na jing* (Sūtra of Prince Sudāna), one fascicle, sixteen sheets;
translated by Faqian during the Western Qin dynasty. *Taizi mupo jing* (Sūtra of Prince Mūpaka), one fascicle, five sheets.
*The Sūtra of Sudhana* (Xiulaiding jing), one fascicle, nineteen sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
*The Sūtra of King Suvarṇavarṇa* (Jinsewang jing), one fascicle, eight sheets; translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.

*The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Sole Realization and Self-Vow* (Duzheng zishi samadijing), one fascicle—also known as the *Sūtra on the Tathāgata’s Self-Vow Samādhi* (Rulai zishi samadijing)—eight sheets; translated by [Kumārajīva] during the Later Wei dynasty.
The *Mahāmāyā Sūtra*, three fascicles and twenty-five sheets, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty;
the *Mahāvaipulyatathāgatagarbha Sūtra*, one fascicle and nine sheets, translated by Tanying during the Southern Qi dynasty;
and the *Tathāgata-upāyakauśalyamantra Sūtra*, one fascicle and eleven sheets, translated by Buddhabhadra during the Yixi era of the Jin dynasty.
One fascicle of the *Śrīmālādevī-siṃhanāda-ekayāna-mahopāya-sūtra*, translated by Guṇabhadra during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty; nineteen sheets.
One fascicle of the *Sūmatiparipṛcchā-bodhisattva-sūtra*, also known as the *Sūmatī-sūtra*, translated by Guṇavarman at Yangzhou during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty; eight sheets.
One fascicle of the *Adbhuta-guṇa-parivarta-sūtra*, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty; six sheets.
One fascicle of the *Śiriṣa-mañjarī-bodhisattva-sūtra*, translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty; five sheets.
One fascicle of the *Kṣemavatī-vyākaraṇa-sūtra*, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty; four sheets.
One fascicle of the *Candraprabha-bodhisattva-sūtra*, translated by Dharmaruci during the Later Wei dynasty; three sheets.
*The Scripture on the Extinction of Darkness in the Ten Directions*, one fascicle, six sheets, translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty;
*The Scripture on the Arising of the Bodhisattva Mind*, one fascicle, eleven sheets, translated by Zhu Fahu during the Yuanxi era of the Jin dynasty;
and [the scripture] translated by Jñānagupta, Dharmagupta, and others at Daxingshan Monastery during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
One scroll of the *Pumenpin jing* (Universal Gate Chapter Sutra), twelve sheets;
translated by Zhu Fahu during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty. One scroll of the *Pusa shizhu jing* (Sutra on the Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva), fourteen sheets;
translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty. One scroll of the *Shangzhuntianzi jing* (Sutra of the Devaputra Merchant Leader), sixteen sheets.
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, Śīladharma (Jñānagupta) and Dharmagupta (Gupta) and others translated at Daxingshan Temple the *Cittavidyā-sūtra* (Heart-Clarifying Scripture),
one fascicle, three sheets, which was subsequently promulgated by imperial decree of the Tang court.

Also, during the Jin dynasty, Dharmarakṣa translated the *Candrapradīpa-samādhi-sūtra* (Moon-Lamp Samādhi Scripture), one fascicle— also known as the *Mañjuśrī-bodhisattva-daśakriyā-sūtra* or the *Pratibhāna-prajñā-samādhi-sūtra*— ten sheets.

*The Sūtra Spoken by the Bodhisattva Acintyaprabha*, one fascicle, also titled *The Sūtra of the Coughing Child Bodhisattva Acintyaprabha*; translated during the Song dynasty by Master Xian, twelve sheets.

*The Sūtra on the Questions of Mañjuśrī Regarding the Bodhisattva Stations*, one fascicle, also titled *The Sūtra on the Questions of Stations*; translated during the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu, twenty sheets.

*The Sūtra of Prince Śrīprabha*, one fascicle, also titled *The Sūtra of the Questions of Rāṣṭrapāla Regarding Prince Śrīprabha*; translated during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han by Zhi Chen, nineteen sheets.
*The Sūtra on the Merit of Offering Lamps*, one fascicle, fourteen sheets, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taishi era of the Jin dynasty;
*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Condemnation of Lust*, one fascicle, two sheets, translated by [Guṇabhadra] during the Qi dynasty;
*The Sūtra on Human Desire and Birth*, one fascicle, fourteen sheets, translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
*Ren suocailai jing* (Sūtra on Where People Come From), one fascicle, translated by An Shigao during the reign of Emperor Huan of the Later Han; the original text was lost.
*Buzengbujian jing* (Sūtra of Neither Increase nor Decrease), one fascicle, six pages, translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.
*Foyu jing* (Sūtra of the Buddha’s Words), one fascicle, three pages, translated by [Kumārajīva] during the Later Wei dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Jewel Casket Without Letters*, one fascicle, six sheets; translated during the Later Wei dynasty by Bodhiruci.
*The Sūtra of the Tathāgata’s Lion’s Roar*, one fascicle, five sheets; translated during the Later Wei dynasty by Bodhiruci.
*The Sūtra of the Ten Dharmas*, one fascicle, twenty sheets; translated during the Later Wei dynasty by Bodhiruci together with Buddhasanta.
*Aniyatapraveśa-sūtra* (一卷), twenty-one pages, translated by Saṃghabara in Yangzhou during the Putong era of the Liang dynasty;
*Dvādaśabuddhanāma-mantra-sūtra* (一卷), six pages, translated by Dharmaruci during the Northern Wei period;
*Mārakarma-parivarta-sūtra* (一卷), eighteen pages, translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaiguang era of the Sui dynasty.
*Ji zhū fāngděng xué jīng* (Sūtra on Saving Those Who Study the Vaipulya), one fascicle, fourteen sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty.
*Bōsà xíng wǔshí yuánshēn jīng* (Sūtra on the Fifty Circumstances of the Bodhisattva’s Practice of the Body), one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
*Nèizàng bǎibǎo jīng* (Sūtra of the Hundred Treasures of the Inner Treasury), one fascicle, eight sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
During the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty, Zhi Qian translated the *Mahāvaipulya-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in one fascicle, comprising thirteen sheets of paper.
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, Vinītāruci translated the *Maitreya-bodhisattva-paripṛcchita-pūrvapraṇidhāna-sūtra* in one fascicle, comprising eight sheets of paper.
During the Jin dynasty, Dharmarakṣa translated the *Mañjuśrī-bhāṣita-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* in one fascicle, comprising twenty-two sheets of paper.
*The Sūtra of the Firm Woman*, one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Man-tuo during the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Exposition of the Deeds of the Laity and the Clergy*, one fascicle, nine sheets; translated by Yaśas during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Birthplace of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle—also known as the *Carmavastu Sūtra*—three sheets; translated by Fa-jian during the reign of the Western Qin dynasty.

*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Way under the Tree*, one fascicle, translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty; also known as the *Sīhāméi Sūtra* or the *Dàoshù Sānmèi Sūtra*; eleven pages.
Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty. *The Jewel Net Sūtra*, one fascicle, also known as the *Jewel Net Youth Sūtra*;
twenty-three pages. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Names of One Hundred Buddhas*, one fascicle; six pages.
*The Sūtra of Immeasurable Meanings*, one fascicle, seventeen sheets; translated by Dharmayaśas during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
*The Sūtra on Contemplating Maitreya’s Ascent to Tuṣita Heaven*, one fascicle, eight sheets; translated by Dharmagatayaśas in Yangzhou during the Jianyuan era of the Southern Qi dynasty.
*The Sūtra on Contemplating the Buddha of Immeasurable Life*, one fascicle, sixteen sheets; translated by An-yang Hou Juqu Jingsheng during the Northern Liang period.

In the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty, Jñānayaśas translated the *Bhadracaryā-praṇidhāna-sūtra* (The Scripture on the Practice of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra) in one fascicle, consisting of sixteen sheets.

In the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty, Dharmamitra translated the *Bhaiṣajyarāja-bhaiṣajyasamudgata-bodhisattva-sūtra* (The Scripture on the Two Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata) in one fascicle, consisting of nineteen sheets.

In the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty, Jñānayaśas translated the *Avalokiteśvara-viṣanirghāta-dhāraṇī-sūtra* (The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī for Invoking Avalokiteśvara to Eliminate and Subdue Poisonous Harm) in one fascicle, consisting of eleven sheets.
*The Sūtra on the Prediction of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle, fourteen sheets; translated by the foreign master Zhu Nanti during the Song dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Doe Mother*, one fascicle, four sheets; translated by Dharmakṣema at Yangzhou during the Song dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Deer Son*, one fascicle, three sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
*Jue kong zai huan jing* (Sutra on Eliminating Fear and Calamity), one fascicle, fifteen sheets; translated by Zhi Qian during the Jianxing era of the Wu dynasty.
*Wen shi xi yu zhong seng jing* (Sutra on Bathing the Assembly of Monks in a Warm Chamber), one fascicle, three sheets; translated by Bai Yan during the Wei dynasty.
*Si bu ke de jing* (Sutra on the Four Unobtainables), one fascicle, four sheets; translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.

*Zhude fudian jing* (Sutra on the Fields of Merit for the Virtuous), one fascicle; translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty; also known as *Fudian jing*, six sheets. Translated by Faju during the Jin dynasty:
*Chujia gongde jing* (Sutra on the Merit of Leaving Home), one fascicle, five sheets.
Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty: *Rufa jie tixing jing* (Sutra on the Essential Nature of Entering the Dharma Realm), one fascicle, ten sheets.
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, Jñānagupta translated at Daxingshan Temple the following works, which were subsequently presented for imperial circulation:

*The Scripture on the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha Asking about the Retention of How Much Merit* in one fascicle and six sheets; *The Scripture on the Practice of Bodhisattvas*, also titled *The Scripture on the Elder Mahātejas Observing the Practice of the Body*, in seven sheets;
*The Scripture on the Causes and Conditions of the Bodhisattva Throwing Himself to a Starving Tiger and Erecting a Stūpa* in seven sheets; and *The Dana-pāramitā Practiced by All Donors*.

*Maitreyabuddhotpādasūtra*, one fascicle, seventeen sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *Maitreyaparivartasūtra* (also known as *Maitreyavyākaraṇasūtra*), one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Kumārajīva in the Hongshi era of the Later Qin. *Maitreyāgamanasūtra*, one fascicle, three sheets; a missing text now recovered. The above three sūtras are the same work translated differently.

*Amoghapāśa Sūtra*, one fascicle, ten sheets; translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty. *Amoghapāśa Divine Mantra Sūtra*, one fascicle, twelve sheets; translated by Xuanzang during the Zhenguan era of the Tang dynasty. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*The Shorter Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, one fascicle, four pages; translated by Guṇabhadra during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty. *The Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, one fascicle, five pages; translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty. The two sūtras above are the same text with different translations.

Translated by Xuanzang during the Tang dynasty. The above three scriptures are the same original text with different translations.

*The Scripture of the Old Mother*, one fascicle; also titled *The Scripture of the Old Woman*, two sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty. *The Scripture of the Six Virtues of the Old Mother*, one fascicle, two sheets. The above two scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Mañjuśrīparipṛcchāsūtra*, one fascicle, five sheets; translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty. *Mañjuśrīcarita-sūtra*, one fascicle, seven sheets; translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*Vajrarasottama-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle, fourteen sheets; translated during the Later Wei dynasty by Buddhayaśas. *Vajramaṇḍala-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle, fourteen sheets; translated during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty by Jñānagupta. *Zheng gongjing jing* (Sūtra on Proper Reverence), one fascicle, five sheets; translated by Buddhayaśas during the Later Wei dynasty. *Shan gongjing jing* (Sūtra on Good Reverence), one fascicle, seven sheets; translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty. The two sūtras above are the same text with different translations.

*The Sūtra of the Girl Vimaladattā*, one fascicle, twenty-four sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Vimaladattā’s Discernment of Responsive Eloquence*, one fascicle, twenty-two sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin period. *The Sūtra of the Girl Vimalāprāptā*, one fascicle, twenty-five sheets; a missing text now recovered, translated by Gautama Rajyaghosa at Xiangzhou during the Xinghe era of the Later Wei dynasty. The above three sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Scripture of the Girl Abhayamati*, one fascicle, twenty-five sheets; translated by Buddhayaśas during the Yuanxiang era of the Later Wei. *The Scripture of the Bodhisattva Ajātaśatru’s Daughter Arthadā*, one fascicle, seventeen sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. These two scriptures above are translations of the same original text.

*Mahāyāna Vaipulya Essential Wisdom Sūtra*, one fascicle, one page; *Sūtra on the Questions of Maitreya Bodhisattva*, one fascicle, four pages; translated by Dharmaruci during the Later Wei period. *Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Seal of Wisdom*, one fascicle, twenty-one pages; translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu period. *Tathāgata-jñāna-mudrā Sūtra*, one fascicle, nineteen pages. *Jueding zongchi jing* (Sutra on the Definitive Dhāraṇī), one fascicle, eight sheets; also titled *Jue zongchi*. The above two sutras are the same text with different translations.

*The Sūtra of the Buddha Kṣīrarasmi*, one fascicle, six pages; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Vatsagotra*, one fascicle, two pages. The above two sūtras are the same text with different translations.

*The Buddha’s Bequeathed Sun-Maṇi Jewel Sūtra*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets; translated by Zhi Chen during the Guanghe era of the Later Han. *The Great Jewel Accumulation Sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-one sheets. *The Mahāyāna Jewel Adornment Sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty sheets. These three sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle; twelve sheets; translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty. *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle; fourteen sheets; translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle; fourteen sheets; translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty. *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle; nineteen sheets; translated by Xuanzang during the Tang dynasty. The above four sūtras are the same original text translated differently.

*Jiāzhǎngzǐ zhì jīng* (The Scripture on the Elder’s Son’s Restriction), also titled *Zhì jīng*, one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Zhī Fǎdù during the Jìn dynasty. *Shì tóngzǐ jīng* (The Scripture of the Departing Youth), one fascicle, two sheets; translated by Zhī Fǎdù during the Jìn dynasty. *Bōsà shì jīng* (The Scripture of the Bodhisattva’s Departure), also titled *Shì jīng*, one fascicle, four sheets. *The Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-bodhicitta-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra on the Non-activity of Bodhi*, seven pages. Translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Hastikṣetra-vihāra-sūtra*, one fascicle, nine pages. Translated by Vinitaruci during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty. The above three sūtras are translations of the same original text with different translations.

*Fǎpǔyì jīng* (Sūtra on the Meaning of the Universal Dharma), one fascicle; also titled *Jùfǎxíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Practice of Endowed Dharmas), nine sheets;

translated during the Jin dynasty by the śramaṇas Faju and Falì. *Dàpānniéhuán jīng* (Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra), two fascicles; this is the *Xiáyóuxíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Wandering), forty-eight sheets.

The *Buddha-parinirvāṇa Sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty; also the *Caryā-sūtra* in fifty-five sheets, translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
the *Śikhālavya-ṣaḍ-abhimukha-praṇāma Sūtra* in one fascicle—also known as the *Mahā-ṣaṭpada-praṇāma Sūtra*—in four sheets, translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
and the *Brahmajāla-dvāṣaṣṭi-dṛṣṭi Sūtra* in one fascicle—also known as the *Brahmajāla Sūtra*—in twenty sheets.

twenty-seven sheets. The *Śramaṇaphala-sūtra* in one fascicle, translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty; sixteen sheets. *Benxiang yi zhi jing* (Sūtra on the Mutual Reliance of the Fundamental Characteristics), one fascicle, two sheets; translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty. *Yuan ben zhi jing* (Sūtra on the Conditions of the Fundamental Basis), one fascicle, three sheets. The *Sūtra of the Five Mothers and Sons*, one fascicle, two sheets; the *Śrāmaṇera-luo Sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets. These two sūtras above are the same text with different translations. The *Asudā Sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets;

The *Maudgalyāyanī-sūtra*, one fascicle—also titled the *Mātangī-sūtra* or the *Sūtra Spoken by Ānanda on Being Affected by Sorcery*—three sheets. *The Sutra on the Seal of the Noble Dharma* (Āryadharmamudrā-sūtra). One fascicle. Two sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han Dynasty.
